newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 29.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Experts consider the slight improvement in the foreign trade balance during the first quarter of this year positive. They warn, however, that it should not be overestimated.
- From May 15, CS-Stavebni Sporitelna will decrease by one percent its interest rates for mid-term bridging credits which citizens can obtain for housing.
- Trade Minister Martin Riman said the only way to uphold the cabinet's new economic measures is to lay off more employees from Czech Railways than originally expected.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - According to the most recent survey from IVVM, only 24 percent of the 11,000 Czechs asked are satisfied with politics in their country, 10 percent less than in March.

PRAVO - The police are prepared to ensure a calm visit for German President Roman Herzog today in Prague. Herzog will address the Czech parliament, and there is hope that the Republicans will not disrupt the meeting.
- On Monday, the crown reached an all-time record low when it dropped to 3.8 percent below parity. Before that the record low was 2.7 percent.
- Ceska Sporitelna had net profits of 632 million crowns for the first quarter of this year.
- From May 1, brewery Radegast will increase its prices of all its beers by between seven and nine percent.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Union workers at Motol Hospital in Prague will begin a five-day strike tomorrow, protesting against the dismissal of leading heart sergeon Josef Dvorak by Health Minister Jan Strasky.
- Zivnostenska Banka had net profits last year of 378 million crowns, a decrease of seven percent in comparison to 1995.
